Each plugin is a self-contained module implementing the VystedPlugin interface and declaring which capabilities it contributes.
Capability negotiation means panels/commands/agents that a plugin doesn't provide are gracefully omitted.
VystedPlugin interface declares identity: pluginId, pluginName, pluginType, version.
VystedPlugin interface declares lifecycle methods: initialize, shutdown, healthCheck.
VystedPlugin interface declares capabilities: contributesData, contributesPanels, contributesCommands, contributesAgents, contributesNodes, supportsControlPlane.
VystedPlugin interface supports data contribution via getDataSources().
VystedPlugin interface supports panel contribution via getPanels().
VystedPlugin interface supports command-bar (slash command) contribution via getCommands().
VystedPlugin interface supports AI agent contribution via getAgents().
VystedPlugin interface supports node-editor contribution via getNodes().
VystedPlugin interface supports real-time subscriptions via subscribe(channel, callback), if supported.
VystedPlugin interface supports a control plane via executeCommand(commandId, args), if supported.
Tradesa V2 plugin implements all six VystedPlugin capabilities.
OpenBB ODP wrap plugin implements only contributesData.
Future plugins pick whichever capabilities fit.
AI sandboxability has three layers: per-panel context, specialized workflow agents, and multi-agent orchestration via node editor.
Every panel that benefits from AI has an inline AI sidebar/chat (Layer 1).
The Layer-1 AI agent knows the panel's context (current ticker, current chart timeframe, current portfolio).
Example behaviour: user opens an AAPL chart and the AI knows AAPL is the context.

From v1.0, Vysted Terminal places live orders against real brokerage accounts.
Vysted Terminal is a tool, not financial advice — nothing it displays, computes, or generates, including AI-agent output, is a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any instrument.

No warranty for trading losses — the AGPL-3.0 disclaimer (§15-16) is explicitly extended to trading and financial losses, including losses from defects, data errors, latency, failed or duplicated orders, or AI-agent behaviour.
The user owns the broker relationship — Vysted Terminal is not a broker, introducing broker, or investment adviser.
COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md mirrors the trading-loss disclaimer with an explicit no-warranty-for-trading-losses clause.
Live order placement is gated behind a fixed set of safeguards that are non-negotiable design constraints for every broker plugin; no broker plugin ships without them.
Paper mode is the default for every broker plugin.
Live trading is opt-in per broker, toggled by the user.
The first time a plugin is switched to live, a dedicated disclaimer dialog is shown and must be explicitly acknowledged.
There is no global 'enable everything' shortcut for live trading — the decision is made one broker at a time.
Every order, paper or live, requires a confirmation dialog showing symbol, quantity, side, order type, limit price, estimated value, broker, and account ID.
There are no one-click trades anywhere in the app, in any panel, for any broker.
Position-size limits are configurable per plugin, with soft default caps on maximum order value, maximum percentage of account, and maximum position size per symbol.
A user can raise a position-size limit only through an explicit confirmation step; the defaults are conservative on purpose.
Every order, manual or AI-initiated, is written to a local SQLite audit log with timestamp, broker, full request payload, broker response, and outcome.
The audit log is exportable and survives app restarts.
There is a global 'Halt All Trading' kill switch, always visible, that immediately disables order placement across every broker plugin at once.
The kill switch is designed to be found and used under stress, without hunting through settings.
When an AI agent or node-editor workflow attempts to place an order, the confirmation dialog opens defaulted to declined and names the agent (e.g. 'AI agent <name> is requesting this order').
An optional auto-approve mode for AI-initiated orders exists but is off by default and must be enabled explicitly, per agent.
The terminal never lets an AI place an order the user did not see.
Any individual broker plugin can be marked read-only even with live trading globally enabled, enforced at the plugin boundary, not just the UI.
Liability disclaimers are surfaced at four touchpoints: the AGPL-3.0 LICENSE, COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md, the first-launch app TOS dialog, and a per-broker first-connect dialog.
The first-launch app TOS dialog is a one-time acknowledgment the user must accept before any broker plugin can be enabled at all.
A per-broker first-connect dialog shows a broker-specific terms-and-conditions reminder the first time the user connects each broker.
The execution path is conservative by construction: paper by default, confirmed every time, capped, logged, haltable, extra-gated for AI, and disclosed up front.

Use Case 1 (Solo Founder's Quant Day): morning open triggers a Tradesa V2 overnight check (read-only, 7 panels) -> AI Risk Analyst review -> backtest new strategy -> (v0.6.6+ target) push config to bot via the Tradesa plugin control plane.
Use Case 2 (Research Workflow): Cmd+K 'Research XYZ' -> AI Researcher pulls everything -> chart + news in adjacent panels -> backtest dividend strategy -> save workspace.
Use Case 3 (Earnings Playbook): build a node-editor workflow -> AI generates thesis per earnings name -> alert on entry trigger -> desktop notification -> review thesis -> trade externally.

Use Case 4 (Academic Researcher): a custom AI agent fine-tuned to a research domain runs a workflow pulling SEC + sentiment data, outputs to chart, and the workspace becomes a reproducible dissertation methodology.

Use Case 5 (Macro Thesis Watcher, Dalio-style): a workspace with yield curves + central bank tracker + commodity dashboard has an AI Macro Researcher monitor news and send notifications on thesis-confirming events.

Use Case 6 (Plugin Ecosystem, year 2+): indie trading-bot developers implement Vysted's plugin contract, their users get Vysted Terminal as a free dashboard, and Vysted becomes the standard UX layer for open-source trading infrastructure.

Use Case 7 (Multi-Broker Portfolio Aggregation): a user holding positions across Zerodha Kite, Dhan, and Alpaca can pull all three broker plugins into one Vysted workspace with aggregate P&L, per-broker drilldown panels, and cross-broker risk metrics (concentration, correlation, total exposure) computed across the combined book; execution stays per-broker and behind every §6.5 safeguard, with aggregation read-side only.
